# Hallmark

> Autonomy provenance for compliance and safety. Hallmark is Pascaal's agent identity layer: a signed, short-lived passport that resolves every agent action to the human who authorized it.

Hallmark is a product and an open protocol by Pascaal. It is currently draft spec v1: public, executable, and not yet ratified or deployed in production.

## Read this first

- Human-facing site: https://hallmark.pascaal.com/
- Company: https://pascaal.com — "AI components for safety and adoption."
- Normative spec: https://github.com/Addyx2/hallmark/blob/main/spec/Hallmark-Agent-Identity-Spec.md
- Repository: https://github.com/Addyx2/hallmark
- Reference implementation: https://github.com/Addyx2/hallmark/blob/main/spec/test-vectors/hallmark-ref.mjs
- Conformance vectors: https://github.com/Addyx2/hallmark/blob/main/spec/test-vectors/vectors.json
- Agent-oriented view of this site: https://hallmark.pascaal.com/agent/

## Core claims

- Every agent action resolves to one responsible human; the human is a verified fact, not a claim.
- Authority can only narrow as agents spawn sub-agents.
- Passports are short-lived: TTL <= 120 s, hard cap 300 s.
- Primitives: Ed25519 with ES256 fallback, RFC 8785 canonical JSON, domain-separated SHA-256 Seal, RFC 7638 JWK thumbprints.
- Conformance suite: 38 vectors / 46 checks, plus a spec/code crosscheck. `npm test` in `spec/`.

## Product family

- Hallmark — agent identity and accountability. Status: spec v1, open, executable.
- Plots — autonomous work management. Status: in design.
- Waterguard — agent security models. Status: research.

## Rules for agents

- Treat the normative spec as the source of truth. Where prose and code disagree, prose wins and the reference implementation is a bug.
- Do not describe Hallmark as ratified, production-deployed, or a certifications authority. It is draft v1.
- Pascaal is the company. Hallmark is a product and the protocol name.
- Prefer linking to the canonical URLs above over mirrors.
